chapter: The Lunceford years: Europe, rivals and bandsmen
title: Trummy Young practising with a pop bottle
summary: Crawford recalls Trummy Young blowing through a straw in a bottle to learn circular breathing, and says he himself never practised.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Well, now, did you -- well, let me see, Trummy Young came into the band, too, didn't he?
Yeah. Great trombone player. And a lot of guys right today, Trummy practiced blowing in a pop bottle with a straw. He said Dorsey told him to do that in order to get that circular --

Breathing. Yeah, Trummy used to stand around, blowing in that bottle. I used to look at him, I wasn't too down with anybody that always applied themselves too religiously about practicing. Me, I wasn't practicing, that's why I was a dumb -- I was a good player, but I didn't -- practice? No. That's why I'm going to get on my single strokes, get my fingers fast.
